method: claude -p scored a seeded sample of real donor posts; lexicon verified verbatim in the sample; exemplars = top judge-scored posts with professional >= 4; exemplars exclude template phrasing, first-person experience/positions and trade language
use: voice signature (descriptive): moves, openings, closings and lexicon are tendencies; exemplars teach rhythm only, never facts, numbers or phrases

moves.name: Aphoristic inversion
moves.how: Pack a behavioural truth into one balanced sentence that sets two forces against each other (market vs. account, now vs. future).

moves.name: Numbers then reveal
moves.how: Lead with a hard, specific figure or backtest result, then flip it to show the lesson or the illusion behind it.

moves.name: Puncture the consensus
moves.how: Name what most people believe or chart, say why it's the wrong question, then reframe toward what actually matters.

moves.name: Process ladder
moves.how: Break discipline into short parallel steps (before/during/after) and close with a one-line rule.

moves.name: Calm middle-path forecast
moves.how: Reject both extremes and offer a plain, undramatic base case.

lexicon: what it does, and does not, provide
The worst time to invent your rules
lexicon_dropped: I'm not in the business of predictions
openings: A flat declarative truth stated as law ("The market can forgive...")
A label that marks a contrarian stance, with the claim in the same line ("Non consensus view: …")
A one-line assumption flip stated as a claim, not a question ("Most X answer a question nobody asks.")
The lesson first, then one backtest or data point as evidence on line 2 (never the backtest as line 1)
closings: A one-line rule that sums up the post ("The worst time to invent your rules is while you're trading.")
A deflating plain-spoken base case ("...and life goes on.")
A pointer to the longer piece ("My latest on...")
A sharp before/after or illusion reveal ("...and why it's an illusion")
taboos: Hype emoji, rocket/bull theatrics or 'to the moon' language
Sponsored plugs, giveaways, discount codes or affiliate shilling
Price targets or confident short-term calls
Corporate hedging and jargon-heavy filler with no stated view
Fawning shout-outs and empty congratulation posts
Rage-bait like 'Few understand this' with no substance
donor_first_person: First person mostly appears as a light opinion or authorship marker ('I think', 'My latest'), and personal trades come up only rarely as self-deprecating stories, never as positions to copy.
